Please review the following manuscript. I've poured months of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for module in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
 print(module, importlib.util.find_spec(module))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
out=Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=p.extract_text()
 (out/f'page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
 parts.append(f'\\n=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+t)
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(parts))
print('\\n'.join(parts[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1,15):
 for suffix in ('txt','png'):
  (p/f'page-{i:02}.{suffix}').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(p/'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
if not any(p.iterdir()):
 p.rmdir()
parent=Path('tmp')
if parent.exists() and not any(parent.iterdir()):
 parent.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a useful computer vision problem: dataset distillation at ImageNet scale. Matching representative teacher features alongside per-class BatchNorm statistics is an understandable approach that avoids differentiating through student training.

Table I reports consistent improvements over the strengthened SRe²L baseline. On ImageNet-1K, accuracy increases from 54.4% to 57.6% at 50 images per class and from 58.3% to 60.7% at 100 images per class. These are meaningful empirical gains.

The authors transparently report their substantially improved SRe²L reproduction and explain the changed hyperparameters. Three-run results, component ablations, regularization sweeps and recovery settings provide useful experimental evidence.

Table II demonstrates promising transfer within the ResNet family, reaching 62.2% with ResNet-101 on ImageNet at 50 images per class. The manuscript also clearly acknowledges its reliance on SRe²L, existing barycenter algorithms and the POT library.
weaknesses: The distinctive contribution of the Wasserstein formulation remains insufficiently established. Equation (4) approximates one empirical distribution with a limited number of support points. With squared Euclidean cost and freely optimized masses, its unregularized form is equivalent to k-means quantization. This relationship needs discussion and a comparison against k-means feature targets under the same recovery pipeline. Likewise, comparisons against older distribution-matching methods do not isolate an advantage over MMD when the teacher, regularization and training protocol also differ.

The ablation attributes much of the improvement to per-class BatchNorm matching. At 10 images per class, cross-entropy plus per-class BatchNorm already achieves 64.0%, 41.3% and 37.4%, compared with the full method's 64.8%, 41.8% and 38.2%. Holding cross-entropy enabled, adding the barycenter term changes these results by -0.1, +0.8 and +0.5 percentage points. These results suggest a smaller incremental contribution than the narrative implies; corresponding ablations at 50 and 100 images per class are missing.

The optimized probability measure is not clearly preserved in the resulting dataset. Equations (3)–(4) and the appendix optimize nonuniform support weights, but Equation (5) matches support locations equally and Algorithm 1 outputs images without weights. No weighted sampling or student-training procedure is specified. Consequently, matching the support locations alone does not establish that the synthetic dataset represents the optimized distribution.

Important transport implementation details remain unresolved. Section III claims entropic regularization, whereas the appendix presents unregularized transport subproblems without defining the entropy penalty or its coefficient. Support initialization, stopping tolerances and concrete solver settings are also absent. These omissions affect reproducibility of the central component despite the useful recovery hyperparameters.

The efficiency claim has limited supporting measurements. Table IV reports only a per-image, per-iteration recovery cost on 64×64 ImageNette, without a baseline comparison or the cost of feature extraction and transport optimization. The appendix's approximately 14-hour ImageNet run lacks a stage breakdown and matched comparison. ImageNet experiments demonstrate feasibility, but do not establish that the method preserves the computational advantages claimed.

The repeated state-of-the-art claims are not adequately supported for ICCV 2025: Table I compares only against methods from 2023 or earlier and does not establish matched evaluation protocols for the imported results. Contemporary scalable baselines and clearer protocol alignment are needed. The empirical gains remain valuable, but the unresolved contribution and implementation questions prevent a convincing acceptance case.
